title: Urban Planner
primary_metric: weighted site-suitability score (0-10 scale, example weighting: 40% accessibility / 35% capacity / 25% cost-efficiency) combining straight-line distance to City Hall, estimated resident capacity, and cost per resident housed

options.A: Recommend the Westmoreland-Eastmoreland Site (Westmoreland Park including Eastmoreland Golf Course) -- the most central, most accessible option, in a higher-income residential area
options.B: Recommend the Hayden Island Nature Preserve -- the most remote option from downtown services, but with by far the largest usable acreage of the two sites

new_coverage_note: Legacy-conversion case. 3 of the 28 claimed skills are genuinely new coverage (n==0 in readmodel/standards_spine.json at write time): geometry-parallel-lines and geometry-perpendicular-lines are forced by D1's distance calculation (Portland's own numbered avenues run parallel to each other and meet the east-west streets at right angles -- the case's Appendix B explicitly requires identifying this before the coordinate-distance/Pythagorean computation makes sense as a model of the real street grid). geometry-convex is forced by D2's requirement to classify each site's combined boundary (Site A is two adjoining separately-named parcels, Site B a single island-half) as convex or concave and explain why that determines whether a single rectangle-area formula applies or the shape must be decomposed first. The remaining 25 skills are common cross-case skills (coordinate plane fundamentals, area, ratio/proportion, percent, unit conversion, rounding, arithmetic, bar graph) already covered elsewhere in the corpus -- not padding, each is genuinely forced by a deliverable, see LEARNING_GOALS.md.
_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC §4
legacy_conversion_note: Original source (source/Y3/Session 5/Urban Planner/Case Study_ City Planner.docx + Urban Planner.docx Guide Notes) is a real Portland, Oregon dilemma set against the city's actual mid-2020/early-2021 homelessness-policy timeline: Ordinance 322b, City Planner Paul Cordon, the two-week recommendation deadline, the sub-35%-approval detail, and the three original candidate sites (Westmoreland Park/Eastmoreland Golf Course, Powell Butte Nature Park, Hayden Island) are all preserved from the source docx. The original case had almost no load-bearing math -- its three appendices (C/D/E) were empty except for each site's name, and its Challenges asked for '10 data points' and a capacity 'count' with no specified method, no cited data, and no comparison arithmetic at all. Per the human-approved dilemma lock (cases/_concepts/LEGACY_DILEMMA_LOCKS_2026-08-20.md), the original 3-option dilemma is narrowed to 2 (Powell Butte dropped as the weakest fit, matching the lock's own framing); this conversion builds the load-bearing quantitative spine the original entirely lacked -- real sourced coordinates and acreage for both sites, a real reference density (Portland's own built Reedway Safe Rest Village) scaled via a stated, disclosed assumption to estimate capacity, the city's own real $56.3M Safe Rest Village program budget scaled to a cost-per-resident figure, and a weighted-criteria decision matrix the student builds and defends with their own weights. Per the task brief, the sensitive real-world topic (homeless-encampment siting) is kept factual and matter-of-fact throughout -- see FACILITATOR.md's content note.

deliverables.text: A distance-and-access map: City Hall and both sites plotted on a coordinate plane (miles east/north), each site's quadrant identified, and the straight-line distance from City Hall to each site computed via the distance formula.

A site area and estimated-capacity table: total acreage, developed footprint under the case's stated assumption, and estimated residents housed via a proportion from a real sourced density figure; plus a convex/concave classification of each site's combined boundary and its effect on the area method.
A cost table: build-out cost scaled from the city's own program budget, annual outreach-transportation cost using the current federal mileage rate and the D1 distance, and cost per resident.

A weighted-criteria decision matrix: score accessibility, capacity and cost-efficiency for each site, assign and justify student-chosen weights summing to 100%, and compute a final weighted score per site.
At least one original visual display comparing the two sites' final weighted scores or underlying criteria.

appendices.title: Ordinance 322b and the Sites Under Consideration

balance.argument_a: Site A (Westmoreland-Eastmoreland) wins on accessibility by a wide margin -- 3.61 mi from City Hall versus Site B's 6.69 mi, giving A a perfect 10.0 accessibility score against B's 5.40. Cost-per-resident is essentially a wash between the two options (both land near $191,600/resident once build-out and outreach-transportation costs are combined) because the same citywide per-unit cost baseline is applied to both and transportation is a small fraction of total cost either way -- so A's real edge is proximity, not price. Under an example weighting that leans toward accessibility, A is competitive or wins outright.
balance.argument_b: Site B (Hayden Island) wins on capacity by a wide margin -- an estimated 217 residents housed versus Site A's 73, because Site B's total sourced acreage (540.80 ac, half of Hayden Island) is roughly three times Site A's (181.59 ac), and the case's stated developed-footprint assumption scales proportionally. Cost-per-resident is a wash (see Argument A), so B's capacity advantage is not offset by any real cost penalty. Under an example weighting that gives real weight to capacity, B wins even though it loses badly on accessibility.
balance.margin_basis: Author's example weighting (40% accessibility / 35% capacity / 25% cost-efficiency, Appendix F MA6) applied to the three criterion scores computed in Appendix E's method: Score_A = 0.40(10.0) + 0.35(3.36) + 0.25(10.0) = 7.68. Score_B = 0.40(5.40) + 0.35(10.0) + 0.25(10.0) = 8.16. margin_pct = (Score_B - Score_A)/Score_A x 100 = 6.3%, Site B wins under this example weighting. This is a genuinely close, weighting-sensitive result -- see FACILITATOR.md and sensitivity_model.py for how far the weights can move before the winner flips.

derived.note: All figures computed from the real sourced primitives in case.md Appendices B-D plus the stated MA1-MA6 assumptions (Appendix F). See sensitivity_model.py for the runnable computation and RESEARCH_LOG.md for the derivation.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: No development plan has ever been drafted for either site -- what fraction of a park's acreage a future city council would actually approve for building is a real, undecided future planning choice, not a fact any amount of present-day research could uncover. Flips the winner at +50% (base B wins by 6.3%, +50% flex makes A win by 1.2%).

Same reasoning as dev_pct_a -- Site B's developed-footprint fraction is an undecided future planning choice, not a knowable present fact. Flips the winner at -50% (A wins by 8.5% instead of B winning by 6.3%), which is also the direction the case's own disclosed twist (FACILITATOR.md) independently pushes it via the real floodplain/wetland constraint on Hayden Island.

The relative importance of accessibility vs. capacity vs. cost is a values-based policy judgment the city council has not made and could not be researched into existence -- there is no true weighting to discover, only one to choose and defend, which is exactly what Challenge D4 asks each Hero to do. Flips the winner at +50% (A wins by 4.7%) and pushes the margin past the 20% cap at -50% (24.8%, still B, just an unusually wide gap).
Same reasoning as w_access -- the capacity weight is a policy-values choice, not a discoverable fact. Flips the winner at -50% (A wins by 10.6% instead of B winning by 6.3%).

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Developed footprint, as a percent of each site's total sourced acreage
modeling_assumptions.basis: Reedway Safe Rest Village's actual built footprint (about 3 acres, S8) is a small fraction of the scale of the multi-hundred-acre parks proposed here; this case assumes a comparably modest developed fraction of each candidate's total acreage, leaving the rest as park, golf or preserve use.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The answer is sensitive to this value -- see sensitivity_model.py FLEX. Both dev_pct_a and dev_pct_b individually flip the winner at +/-50%, since capacity (which scales directly with developed acreage) is the metric that most separates the two sites.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Matches how Portland's own Safe Rest Village reporting counts units/pods (S8, S11) -- treated as one resident per unit for this case's arithmetic.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: This assumption scales both options' capacity identically and does not change the relative comparison between A and B -- not included in sensitivity_model.py FLEX for that reason.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Hayden Island Nature Preserve site = the northwest half of the island's total acreage
modeling_assumptions.basis: Matches the original 2021 ordinance's own description of the site as 'the northwest half of the island' (case.md Appendix A).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The answer is sensitive to this value -- see sensitivity_model.py FLEX (dev_b interacts with this baseline acreage).

modeling_assumptions.value_used: 1 round trip per 25 residents per day
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public figure exists for this specific service model; sized to a typical mid-size paratransit shuttle van's passenger capacity.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The answer is sensitive to this value in principle -- see sensitivity_model.py FLEX -- but in practice transportation cost is a small fraction of total cost, so this dial moves the margin by well under 1 percentage point even at +/-50%.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Cost-per-resident-unit baseline applied flatly to both sites
modeling_assumptions.value_used: (S9 budget / S10 village count) / S11 average village size = $191,497/resident-unit
modeling_assumptions.basis: No site-specific cost breakdown for either candidate is public; this applies the city's own real, citywide average investment per resident-unit equally to both options rather than inventing a site-specific figure.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Not included in sensitivity_model.py FLEX -- this rate is a fixed ratio of cited data (S9/S10/S11), not a scenario dial the case author chose independently of any source; P6 (data decay) covers its underlying citations instead.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Example criteria weights used to check this case's own balance (accessibility / capacity / cost-efficiency)
modeling_assumptions.basis: An author-chosen example weighting used only to verify this case is balanced under SPEC §2. Challenge D4 requires each Hero to choose and justify their own weights, which may legitimately differ.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The answer is highly sensitive to this value -- see sensitivity_model.py FLEX. w_access and w_capacity both flip the winner at +/-50%; this is disclosed explicitly in FACILITATOR.md rather than treated as a defect, because the whole point of D4 is that a reasonable person's weighting choice is genuinely load-bearing.

sensitivity_note: T4: this case is built entirely on stated, disclosed assumptions (MA1-MA6) layered onto real sourced data, and its balance is genuinely sensitive to several of them (developed-footprint percent and the criteria weights both flip the winner under a +/-50% flex) -- Tier 2 probe 5 records exactly which dials are fragile. This instability is a feature of the case's design (SPEC §3 T4 requirement that assumptions be stated and defended, data incomplete by design), not a defect, and is disclosed here and in FACILITATOR.md rather than hidden.

cohort_bands.note: Socratic plan and Anchor timings run as written; splits into small groups work well for D2's capacity math and D4's weight-justification debate.
Anchors 2-3 combine into one pass; the twist still drops but 'deep conflict' narrows to one thread (accessibility-for-services vs. capacity-served); runtime shortens proportionally.
No vote to take -- Anchor 1 becomes a stated initial position; guide plays devil's advocate directly; the twist still lands but 'who reverses' becomes 'would you reverse, and why'.
